statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the reachable public entry endpoint. The endpoint redirects through multiple origins and terminates at HTTP 451 with a bare Not Found response, so no additional archetype or primary flow was discoverable.

page.notes: Homepage-only by explicit necessity: DOM, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest, and links were inspected. No internal links, functioning sitemap, forms, app routes, content/detail templates, search, or account flow were available, so those surfaces could not be selected as representative paths. The terminal response itself was fully judged; check-specific contextual absences are recorded as not-applicable.

paths.description: Public entry endpoint and terminal redirect/error archetype. Selected because recon exposed no links, routes, manifest shortcuts, usable sitemap, form, or content template. Not covered: article/detail, listing, search, account, and media flows because the endpoint terminates at HTTP 451 before exposing any of them.

findings.summary: The requested homepage does not communicate a purpose or next action.
findings.evidence: Desktop and crawler screenshots show only “Not Found”; the rendered DOM has 9 text characters, no heading, no navigation, and no links.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a successful homepage response with a descriptive H1, concise purpose statement, and a clear primary action.

findings.summary: No representative primary journey can begin or complete.
findings.evidence: The entry URL redirects across three hosts and HTTP/HTTPS before ending at HTTP 451; the final DOM has zero links, forms, or controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix routing and origin configuration first, then expose and test the primary content or media journey end to end.

findings.summary: The failure state gives no explanation or recovery action.
findings.evidence: The 451 response is rendered as the bare text “Not Found” with no status explanation, retry, home link, or support path.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an honest error page that names the problem and offers retry, home, and support/recovery actions.

findings.summary: The error surface does not honor the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white canvas with black Times text, identical to the light rendering; the DOM has no color-scheme declaration or CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light/dark color schemes in the head and on :root, then use adaptive system colors or light-dark() tokens.

findings.summary: The page offers no navigation or attention cue after the redirect failure.
findings.evidence: DOM and screenshots show no link, heading, landmark, current-location cue, or route back from the final 451 page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic recovery navigation with a clear heading and visually prioritized next step.

findings.summary: The page lacks a viewport meta tag and is rendered as a 980 CSS-pixel desktop canvas on mobile.
findings.evidence: At a 360×800 viewport, layout reports hasViewportMeta=false and clientWidth=980 with scale 0.367; the text is visibly tiny in the mobile screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and use fluid, intrinsic sizing for the restored layout.

findings.summary: Origin routing creates a wasteful redirect chain and insecure scheme oscillation.
findings.evidence: HAR records 301 a→g, 302 g→http://6porno365.run, then 307 HTTP→HTTPS and 307 HTTPS→HTTP before the 451 response; 5 of 6 requests are cross-origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical HTTPS origin, redirect to it once, and return a successful cacheable document without scheme loops.

findings.summary: The failure document has no semantic structure.
findings.evidence: The detailed probe finds zero headings and zero landmarks; the DOM is only html/head/body text, so assistive-technology users receive no page structure or recovery navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a descriptive title and H1 inside main, plus semantic navigation for recovery actions.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow starts from a desktop-width layout because viewport configuration is absent.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout uses a 980px layout viewport at device width 360 and the mobile screenshot shows extremely small text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scaling-permissive viewport meta tag and verify reflow and text sizing at narrow widths and zoom.

findings.summary: The served error document is not a sound HTML document.
findings.evidence: The detailed probe reports doctype=null, no head metadata, and no viewport; outerHTML is only <html><head></head><body>Not Found</body></html>.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a standards-mode HTML document with <!doctype html>, charset, viewport, title, and semantic body structure.

findings.summary: The public entry page has neither a title nor meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM and discoverability evidence report an empty title and no meta description in both rendered and raw responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique descriptive title and concise meta description to the successful canonical page and error templates.

findings.summary: The endpoint is neither successfully crawlable nor mobile configured.
findings.evidence: The final document is HTTP 451 with no links or viewport meta. robots.txt points Host and Sitemap at porno365.plus rather than the audited or final origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a 200 canonical HTTPS page, add viewport metadata and crawlable descriptive links, and align robots.txt with the canonical host.

findings.summary: Canonical and indexing signals conflict or fail.
findings.evidence: The document has no canonical URL; sitemap.xml on the final host returns 451; robots.txt advertises a different host; the document itself returns 451.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate to one HTTPS canonical origin, publish a working sitemap, align robots directives, and return successful status codes for public pages.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes no share-preview or structured site metadata.
findings.evidence: The recon probe finds no Open Graph metadata and no JSON-LD while the endpoint is intended as a public homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: After restoring visible content, add accurate Open Graph metadata and appropriate WebSite/Organization JSON-LD.

findings.summary: Transport and cookie security are materially misconfigured.
findings.evidence: Navigation downgrades from HTTPS to HTTP; CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent. All four first-party cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the entire redirect and delivery path on HTTPS, set Secure/SameSite cookies, and deploy baseline security headers beginning with HSTS and a staged CSP.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no HSTS, clickjacking defense, CSP frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out HSTS, CSP including frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content is unavailable rather than progressively enhanced.
findings.evidence: Raw fetch and JavaScript-rendered views both contain only “Not Found”; discoverability reports fetchedStatus=451 and renderedEmpty=true.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful core HTML from the canonical origin before layering client-side enhancements.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling is a dead end.
findings.evidence: A 451 terminal response is shown as “Not Found” with no truthful status context, retry, alternate route, or support action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a resilient server-rendered failure template with accurate status messaging and actionable recovery options.

findings.summary: The document does not declare its language or direction.
findings.evidence: The detailed probe reports htmlLang="" and htmlDir=""; the DOM contains no lang or dir attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set the correct BCP 47 lang value and rely on logical CSS properties in the restored layout.

findings.summary: Nearly all network work is redirect overhead with no user value.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 5 of 6 requests and 5,548 of 5,675 transferred bytes attributed to other origins, mostly the broken redirect chain and favicon, while no content is delivered.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate cross-origin redirect churn and defer non-essential requests until the canonical content response is healthy.
